It really depends which country in Europe. Here in Poland it's pretty grand - I pay $13 for 65Mb up 6Mb down, static public IP, via Ethernet, But you can get 250Mb/20 for $23, as long as you're in an Urban area with Cable, and then you have up to 23Mbit ADSL2+ for cheapo, no data caps on any of them, some of them have public IPv4, some of them IPv6. And then you get really good deals on LTE too, where coverage allows (quickly expanding). AFAIK other Central Europe countries are on par level, with Estonia taking the absolute lead. Good places are also Norway, Sweden and Germany. Then you have UK and parts of France which are mid tier, and then France (the bad parts) and Portugal which are very shit tier. General rule, if you have cable - you're good, and prices depend on how many operators you can choose from. Outside of those places you have ADSL2. Not sure about the FTTH situation.

It was a 'standard' cargo mission to the International Space Station - NASA have contracted billions out to a private company called SpaceX owned by Elon musk to ferry food, oxygen and water (and other stuff).

The idea is that rather than building spaceships for mundane tasks, NASA give money to these private companies to do it instead, meaning that NASA can focus on building the next gen space shuttle replacement.

SpaceX have done 6 successful deliveries (all unmanned) and are starting to test the tech needed to 'convert' their ship to a manned version. But it's more amitious than that - they want to make a fully reusable rocket to bring cost down.

So, this launch, CRS 7, was another unmanned cargo run to the space station, with a secondary goal of landing the first stage of the rocket (the massive rocket itself) on a barge in the ocean.
